chunk_map.heading: H1/lede: Map the access surface, own the delta
Take the ranked ten, leave the rest on disk
Phase 1: Run the curated skill on your feature and save the map
Point the skill at your feature
Kick off the pass, then work the other window
Phase 2: Read the map back before you decide the delta
Phase 3: Add the surface the skill over-called, and the one it missed
Push back until the reason names your codebase
Phase 4: Add the context header a cold reader needs

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest candidate: chunk 1 "Take the ranked ten..." line 19 "The file holds the rest until a decision needs it." — "The file" resolves against "the saved map" named one sentence earlier in the same chunk (line 18: "the saved map first"), same-chunk antecedent, not a violation. Also checked: "STRIDE" (chunk 1 L17 "the STRIDE walk") resolves via chunk 0 L11 (prior context, all chunks); "m3-quality"/"m3-security" (chunk 4 L51-52) self-name on first use in the same chunk; "the delta" (chunks 4, 6, 7) resolves via chunk 0's title and "What you build" line (L9), reused arc-earned vocabulary. No unresolved pronoun/demonstrative found in any chunk.

Closest candidate: chunk 3 line 47 "The plan path you noted at Module 2's close is the best input here" — locates a fact inside another module by position ("at Module 2's close"). Checked against the enclosing module file: `curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/earn-the-trust.md:12` states the identical fact in this module's own Prework ("you noted the path at M2 close"), so the module's own signposting already established this as prior context before the exercise is reached (module include-order carve-out, §1). Independently corroborated in `plan-mode-done-right.md:177`'s artefact-contracts row, confirming the beat is real, not invented. "The countermove from M1" (chunk 1, L18) unpacks its claim in the same sentence ("tell the agent what output you want") — passes the named-not-located test. "Open the side quest" and "Author your test-strategy skill" (chunk 4, L51-52) are named by title, not located by position.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: "Open the side quest" (chunk 4, L52) verified: `curriculum/exercises/open-the-side-quest.md` exists and is included immediately before this file in `earn-the-trust.md`'s Start Here list (line 33 vs line 37). "The plan path you noted at Module 2's close" (chunk 3, L47) verified against `plan-mode-done-right.md:177` ("student notes it at module close for M3 reference") — the beat exists in M2's own file.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No guess-before-reveal / live-demo instruction pattern anywhere in the body — this is a skill-invocation-and-review exercise, not a prediction beat.

Closest candidate: chunk 7 "Push back until the reason names your codebase" (lines 80-82) — single bullet, but carries a full self-standing claim plus a worked contrast example ("'The billing webhook re-hits the queue on retry...' beats 'webhooks need auth.'"), not a bare wait-state. Chunk 4 (lines 49-52, the other short chunk) carries two substantive bullets on the two-window move. No chunk in the file is content-free or purely context-dependent.

chunk 2 "Phase 1: Run the curated skill on your feature and save the map" (lines 22-39): the header promises two actions (run the skill on the feature; save the map). The chunk's actual content (lines 24-39) only confirms which skills are installed — the `/skills` command and a prompt asking Claude to list installed skills, storage location, and context-load status. Nothing in this chunk invokes the skill on the student's feature or saves anything; that happens in the next `##` chunk, "Point the skill at your feature" (lines 41-47), under a differently-worded header. Under the projected sequential read, the Phase 1 slide reads as delivering more than it shows.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Retitle chunk 2 to what it delivers (e.g. "Phase 1: Confirm the skill is on hand"), or fold the invoke-and-save prompt into this chunk so the header's promise lands here.

rules_evaluated.evidence: Checked all five sub-items across all chunks: (a) no "Not X. Not Y. Z." construction found. (b) no anaphora/epistrophe triples found. (c) no self-grading superlative — the closest candidate, chunk 0 L11 "STRIDE without an access-surface map is pub-quiz threat modeling," is a stance claim about the field, not a claim about this exercise's own value (own maintainer block's backing section independently classifies it as a position, not a self-grading assertion). (d) no number-with-retraction pattern present (no numeric claims in body at all). (e) no abstraction-noun-stack or empty-leg verb triplet found — prose stays concrete ("the billing webhook re-hits the queue on retry" style throughout).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: `sed -n '1,96p' curriculum/exercises/map-the-access-surface.md | grep -nEo "writing surface|\bfiring\b|compendium|forcing function|\bbeat\b|\bmood\b|Connections"` → 0 matches in body (all 7 hits for beat/compendium/Connections land at lines 99+, inside the maintainer block, out of scope). "Surface"/"access surface"/"surface map" used throughout as ordinary security-engineering vocabulary (attack-surface analogue), not the compendium's banned authorial-jargon sense ("writing surface"). "Delta" is ordinary engineering usage (diff).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Bold in the body is confined to: chunk 0's widget-chrome labels (Time/Window/What you do/What you build/The point — file's own maintainer block, L131, calls these chrome not emphasis, consistent with the widget-field convention used across the corpus); chunk 2's single handle **User** (L33); chunk 6's delta-menu pair **The over-call.** / **The miss.** (L68, L69) — two bolded leads on one slide, but the maintainer block (L131) frames this as a menu of two options a reader scans to pick a side, and each handle is ≤3 words, within the reading-list/menu-slide carve-out (§9) that lifts the ≤1-per-slide budget while the handle-length cap still holds. No bolded-lead monoculture (bullets elsewhere in the file are plain prose).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content — verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: `grep -n 'map-the-access-surface' curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/earn-the-trust.md` → line 37: `[Exercise: Map the access surface](exercises/map-the-access-surface.md)`, a standard exercise include-link inside the module's `## Start here` section, which wraps in `.phase--exercise` per the pattern `buildDeckModel` requires (verified against the sibling `open-the-side-quest.md` slides instance, which confirmed the same include shape reaches the deck). No phase-less prose section in this file that could be silently dropped.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Numbering — position is computed, content ordinals are linted.
rules_evaluated.evidence: `node scripts/check-slide-numbering.js --file curriculum/exercises/map-the-access-surface.md` → "OK — 1 files, Phase/Step numbering consistent." Phase 1/2/3/4 headers (lines 22, 54, 63, 84) run consecutive; the un-numbered headers between/around them ("Point the skill at your feature", "Take the ranked ten...", "Kick off the pass...", "Push back...", "What this sets up") are plain section titles, not part of the Phase-N scheme, so they owe no ordinal.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 8 of 9 `##` headings are unambiguously imperative ("Take the ranked ten...", "Point the skill at your feature", "Kick off the pass...", "Push back until...") or "Phase N:" + imperative labels. Closest candidate: chunk 9 "What this sets up" (line 93) is neither imperative nor a Phase label, but it also asserts no generalizable claim/law (unlike the compendium's declarative specimens, e.g. "Anything can be reverse-engineered") — it is a navigational segue label pointing at the next exercise. `grep -rn "^## What this sets up" curriculum/exercises/*.md` shows the identical heading reused verbatim in `author-test-strategy-skill.md:69`, confirming it is a repeated closer-label convention across the exercise library, not a one-off ambiguity. No mood confusion present (it does not read as a law the student is meant to carry forward).
